commands.review_summary:
The PR adds stable OTEL diagnostic log and trusted security event identity fields, logger-derived category/site semantics, heartbeat log metadata, exporter/logger coverage, an inventory test, and docs for the exported log shape.

PR surface: Source +733, Tests +747, Docs +16. Total +1496 across 12 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the behavior gap from source: current main emits uncaptured diagnostic log bodies as `log` without top-level `eventName` or reserved `openclaw.log.*` identity fields. I did not run live proof in this read-only review, but the PR body includes redacted live Gateway stdout JSONL examples.

target.title: improve: enrich OTEL log records with stable identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can keep OTEL diagnostic log bodies private today, but redacted records need stable structure to stay useful. This PR makes ordinary `log.record` diagnostics and trusted `security.event` records queryable by event identity and safe structured attributes without enabling broad log-body capture.

The first version effectively proved heartbeat enrichment because heartbeat had the only curated `logEvent` call sites. This update enumerates the wider logger surface and enriches the central logger path so non-heartbeat subsystem, module, plugin, feature, name, and capability logs also receive stable low-cardinality event/category/site semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostic log export now reserves OpenClaw-owned semantic fields before generic attributes: `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type`, and `openclaw.log.*` event/category/outcome/reason/site attributes. Spoofed generic attributes cannot replace those reserved meanings, and attribute-count pressure cannot drop the semantic fields.

Ordinary logs remain redacted by default. Explicit call-site semantics still win when present, but generic logger records now fall back to safe category + code-owner + severity identity and an opaque `openclaw.log.site_id`; trusted `security.event` records stay separate from message-body semantics and keep the structured `openclaw.security.*` schema while adding `openclaw.security.<action>` event identity.

## User Impact

Operators can query exported OpenClaw OTEL logs without parsing message text or enabling broad content capture. The current source census covered by the inventory/audit pass is:

- 9,768 production TS/TSX files scanned under `src`, `extensions`, `packages`, and `ui`.
- 258 logger factories found, including subsystem loggers, child loggers, and plugin/runtime child logger calls.
- 1,077 AST-enumerated categorized logger calls across 191 known logger categories.
- 626 AST-enumerated injected/plugin/free-text logger calls that stay compatible through the generic diagnostic fallback.
- 14 explicit `logEvent` fields, currently 12 unique heartbeat event names.
- 7 trusted security emitter call sites, with helper-routed actions for plugin lifecycle and device/node management.

Current explicit diagnostic event names are heartbeat-owned: `heartbeat.delivery.account_unknown`, `heartbeat.delivery.account_selected`, `heartbeat.delivery.channel_not_ready`, `heartbeat.run.failed`, `heartbeat.runner.agent_run_failed`, `heartbeat.runner.commitment_run_failed`, `heartbeat.runner.disabled`, `heartbeat.runner.started`, `heartbeat.runner.targeted_run_failed`, `heartbeat.schedule.delay_clamped`, `heartbeat.session.archive_failed`, and `heartbeat.wake.deferred`.

All other logger-backed diagnostic records now use the generic event pattern `openclaw.<category>[.<code.function>].<level>` when safe category/function data exists, falling back to `openclaw.log.record` only when no safe logger/category source is available. Subsystem logs now carry the original emitting call site into diagnostics instead of the subsystem file sink wrapper. If an ordinary diagnostic log uses an event beginning with `security.`, its top-level OTEL event name is prefixed as `openclaw.diagnostic.security.*` so only trusted `security.event` records can occupy the `openclaw.security.*` namespace.

Trusted security log actions currently include `security.audit.completed`, `plugin.installed`, `plugin.updated`, `plugin.audit.failed`, `gateway.auth.succeeded`, `gateway.auth.failed`, `tool.execution.blocked`, `exec.approval.requested`, `exec.approval.approved`, `exec.approval.denied`, `device.pairing.denied`, `device.pairing.approved`, `device.pairing.rejected`, `device.pairing.removed`, `device.token.rotation_denied`, `device.token.rotated`, `device.token.revocation_denied`, `device.token.revoked`, `device.role.removed`, and `device.role.removal_denied`.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Redacted `log.record` exports include `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=log.record`, `openclaw.log.event`, `openclaw.log.category`, `openclaw.log.outcome`, `openclaw.log.reason`, and `openclaw.log.site_id` while keeping the body as `[message redacted]`.
- Capture-enabled `log.record` exports keep the same event identity and semantic attributes while replacing only the body with the log message. This mode was used only to prove conditional body behavior; it is not required or recommended for normal operation.
- Trusted `security.event` exports include `eventName=openclaw.security.<action>`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=security.event`, `body=openclaw.security.event`, and the existing `openclaw.security.*` fields.
- Logger tests prove module and plugin/feature child loggers become diagnostic categories with `openclaw.log.category_source`, while generic structured payload fields such as `name` cannot override logger binding categories.
- Subsystem logger tests prove two calls through the same subsystem produce different `openclaw.log.site_id` values from their original source functions, not from the file sink wrapper, and that the trusted source marker is stripped before file output.
- Exporter tests prove ordinary diagnostic logs cannot spoof the trusted `openclaw.security.*` event-name namespace.
- The inventory audit keeps broad OpenClaw logger coverage visible and fails if the production logger/security-event surface drops below the enumerated counts.

Sanitized live local Gateway proof used isolated temp config, fake shared auth token, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`, `diagnostics-otel`, and stdout JSONL log export. Raw temp paths, trace IDs, event IDs, ports, session/account IDs, and token values are intentionally omitted here.

Redacted `log.record` examples from that live Gateway:

```json
{
  "severityText": "INFO",
  "eventName": "openclaw.plugins.start.info",
  "body": "[message redacted]",
  "signalType": "log.record",
  "event": "plugins.start.info",
  "category": "plugins",
  "outcome": "success",
  "reason": "none",
  "siteId": "837e22f502a9a100",
  "bodyRedacted": true,
  "codeFunction": "start"
}
```

```json
{
  "severityText": "INFO",
  "eventName": "openclaw.heartbeat.runner.started",
  "body": "[message redacted]",
  "signalType": "log.record",
  "event": "heartbeat.runner.started",
  "category": "gateway.heartbeat",
  "outcome": "success",
  "reason": "configured",
  "siteId": "959451e6fedb25e7",
  "bodyRedacted": true,
  "codeFunction": "updateConfig"
}
```

```json
{
  "severityText": "DEBUG",
  "eventName": "openclaw.cron.armtimer.debug",
  "body": "[message redacted]",
  "signalType": "log.record",
  "event": "cron.armtimer.debug",
  "category": "cron",
  "outcome": "unknown",
  "reason": "none",
  "siteId": "6216895beaa7d25d",
  "bodyRedacted": true,
  "categorySource": "module",
  "codeFunction": "armTimer"
}
```

Capture-enabled `log.record` examples from a second isolated live Gateway run:

```json
{
  "severityText": "INFO",
  "eventName": "openclaw.plugins.start.info",
  "body": "diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (stdout JSONL)",
  "signalType": "log.record",
  "event": "plugins.start.info",
  "category": "plugins",
  "outcome": "success",
  "reason": "none",
  "siteId": "837e22f502a9a100",
  "codeFunction": "start"
}
```

```json
{
  "severityText": "INFO",
  "eventName": "openclaw.heartbeat.runner.started",
  "body": "heartbeat: started",
  "signalType": "log.record",
  "event": "heartbeat.runner.started",
  "category": "gateway.heartbeat",
  "outcome": "success",
  "reason": "configured",
  "siteId": "959451e6fedb25e7",
  "codeFunction": "updateConfig"
}
```

```json
{
  "severityText": "DEBUG",
  "eventName": "openclaw.cron.armtimer.debug",
  "body": "cron: armTimer skipped - no jobs with nextRunAtMs",
  "signalType": "log.record",
  "event": "cron.armtimer.debug",
  "category": "cron",
  "outcome": "unknown",
  "reason": "none",
  "siteId": "6216895beaa7d25d",
  "categorySource": "module",
  "codeFunction": "armTimer"
}
```

Trusted `security.event` example from the same redacted live Gateway run. This was triggered by a fake CLI WebSocket `connect` request with an intentionally wrong shared token after `diagnostics-otel` reported `logs exporter enabled`:

```json
{
  "severityText": "WARN",
  "eventName": "openclaw.security.gateway.auth.failed",
  "body": "openclaw.security.event",
  "signalType": "security.event",
  "action": "gateway.auth.failed",
  "category": "auth",
  "outcome": "denied",
  "severity": "medium",
  "reason": "token_mismatch",
  "actorKind": "operator",
  "actorRole": "operator",
  "targetKind": "gateway",
  "targetName": "websocket",
  "policyDecision": "deny",
  "controlFamily": "auth",
  "authMode": "token",
  "authMethod": "token",
  "clientMode": "cli"
}
```

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior:

- `src/logging/diagnostic-log-site-inventory.test.ts` enumerates the current production logger/security-event surface and guards the broad source census.
- `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` documents redacted body behavior, semantic log fields, category-source fallback, and separate trusted security event identity.
- Live local Gateway proof on July 1, 2026 covered default-redacted `log.record`, capture-enabled `log.record`, and trusted `security.event` stdout JSONL export using fake auth values and no real channel/provider credentials.

Automated checks:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/talk/logging.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-log-events.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-log-site-inventory.test.ts src/logging/subsystem.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.timeout-warning.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` passed: 6 files, 138 tests across 4 shards.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/subsystem.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-log-events.test.ts` passed after the source-identity patch.
- `pnpm docs:list` passed.
- `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
